chapter_theme: The discourse of the void (சூனிய சம்பாஷணை): seventy riddle verses in the images of farming, cattle, trees, birds, trade and boats, which on their surface describe impossible or puzzling things and are traditionally read as a hidden language for the body, the senses, the breath, the tattvas and the way to Siva. The few plain threads are that the senses must be herded and not let run wild, that the pure path lies overgrown and inverted, and that the sweet is left for the bitter.
structure_note: There is no argued order. Clusters recur: field and plough (2868 to 2880, 2912, 2913), cattle counted in tattva-like numbers (2874, 2875, 2883, 2884, 2903), birds and beasts (2887 to 2893, 2918, 2921), trees and flowers (2898, 2904, 2916, 2917, 2919, 2922, 2928), and trade and the boat (2915, 2929, 2930, 2935). Nearly every verse rests on a code the chapter never states.

2866.reading: With the body as the board, five dice and three eyes, the game is played with the fifty-one letters; the Lord sits there and plays, and I do not know the secret of these magic dice.
2866.nuance: ஐம்பத்தோர் அக்கரம் (fifty-one letters) is the Sanskrit alphabet as mantra theory counts it. கவறு ஐந்து may be the five senses or elements and கண் மூன்று the three lights (sun, moon, fire); these are traditional guesses. The plain sense is that life is a game the Lord plays in the body, and its rule is hidden.

2867.reading: The pure path lies overgrown with brush and no one knows how it lies turned about; for those who do know how it lies turned about, my inner love wells up.
2867.nuance: மாறிக் கிடக்கும் (lies reversed) is repeated and is the key: the path runs against the ordinary direction. Tradition takes it as the yogic turning inward of breath and sight, but the verse only says it is reversed. The verse could stand as a preface to the chapter's riddles.

2868.reading: At a junction where six streets meet there are four palmyras that yield juice; setting a ladder hard to climb, I climbed that palm and saw all seven seas.
2868.nuance: The six streets are traditionally the six adharas, the palm and ladder the central channel climbed by breath, and the seven seas what is seen at the top. None of this is stated; the verse reads as a vision report in farming-village images.

2869.reading: I sowed brinjal and bitter gourd sprouted; I dug the dust and a pumpkin flowered; the garden-folk ran off worshipping, and the banana ripened fully.
2869.nuance: The verse is built on harvests that do not match the sowing. I can't fix what each plant stands for; one reading is that practice yields a fruit other than the one aimed at, and that the full banana ripens after the workers have turned to worship.

2870.reading: There is a field where an elephant grows from the seed called ஐ, and none know that field's clarity; if one gains the mind of the dark-throated Lord, that land is easy to enter without any falsehood.
2870.nuance: ஐ may be a seed-syllable (ஐம் is a known bija), or the word for the subtle or for the master. The elephant from a tiny seed marks the vast fruit of something minute. மையணி கண்டன் is Siva of the dark throat; entry depends on his favour, not on effort.

2871.reading: There is one low field and two high fields, and a thieving field lies mixed among them; for those who plough the field of the heart, it grew of itself into a flooded field.
2871.nuance: The one low and two high fields are sometimes taken as the central and the two side channels, and the thief-field as what steals the yield. உள்ளச்செய், the heart's field, is the one plain term: inner cultivation brings the abundance.

2872.reading: A plough of three yokes ploughs three measures of land and strikes deep to the stake; those who do not yoke the tongue and plough the middle field yoke the breath and plough barren soil.
2872.nuance: நா அணை (tongue-yoke) may mean mantra or a yogic placing of the tongue, கால் அணை (breath-yoke) breath control, and நடு the central channel. களர் (saline, barren land) suggests the breath-ploughers waste their labour, but the verse could also be praising a harder way. I can't settle which.

2873.reading: There are two water-lifts and seven wells; if the water the elder bails and the younger channels does not flow into the beds but runs to waste, it is like a hen raised by a dancing-woman.
2873.nuance: The two lifts are commonly read as the two breaths and the wasted water as breath or vital fluid lost. கூத்தி வளர்த்த கோழி, a dancer's hen, seems proverbial for something raised to no use, but I can't fix the saying.

2874.reading: There are twenty-four penned cows and calves of seven and five; though the calves pour pots of milk, it is the penned cow that suits the Brahmin.
2874.nuance: 24, 7 and 5 add to 36, the Siddhanta count of tattvas, which tradition divides as 24 soul-tattvas, 7 vidya-tattvas and 5 pure tattvas; that fit makes the tattva reading likely. Why the penned cow is preferred, and who the பனவன் is, the verse does not say.

2875.reading: There are twenty-four calving cows, and of the spring-cows one pot of milk is enough; when the wind-cows are milked and drunk, we do not know the coming of the other cows.
2875.nuance: காற்றுப் பசுக்கள் (wind-cows) points to the breath; milking them may be breath control, after which மாற்றுப் பசுக்கள் (the other cows, perhaps births or changes) no longer come. The twenty-four again suggests the tattvas.

2876.reading: On the top floor of the goldsmith's house a bud rose and bloomed red; wanting it round, folding away the truth, the goldsmith seized it.
2876.nuance: The goldsmith is a stock figure of the cheat, and may be the mind; the bud at the top of the house may be a centre in the head. அசுத்தில் is probably a misreading of அகத்தில், as in 2924. I can't give a confident reading.

2877.reading: If, in the sifting seed-bed and the field of trouble, one ties fast the turning water-lift and yokes the good striped milch cow, the cucumber seed spreads and seeds.
2877.nuance: The images (seed-bed, field of trouble, water-lift, cow) are farm work turned to an unstated end; the field of trouble may be the body. The lines are too compressed for a confident reading.

2878.reading: They scatter with a scoop, manure and sow, yoke the ram, stir up the sprout, yet do not cook rice in the big pot and slowly swallow it; that is how they reap red paddy with a ram.
2878.nuance: The rhymes இடா, கிடா, மிடா (scoop, ram, pot) carry the verse. One reading is that they do all the labour and never eat the harvest; the closing line may mock reaping with the wrong tool. Both readings are guesses.

2879.reading: The crop lies ripe, seed for what is above; it lies ripe a league above; for those who reap it again and again, the ripe crop spreads over three leagues.
2879.nuance: விளைந்து (ripened) is repeated seven times. மேலை may be 'above' (the head, in yoga) or 'the hereafter'. காதம் is a measure of distance, and the growth from one to three leagues marks a yield that increases with repeated reaping.

2880.reading: We do not know the intent of those who plough barren land, and they have no intent at all; the young creeper that sprouts in barren land may also wither.
2880.nuance: This takes up களர் உழுவார் from 2872. The verse seems to blame aimless labour on soil that cannot hold a crop, so that even what sprouts dies; what the barren land stands for is not said.

2881.reading: Placing in the fire the wedging noose for the little jackal in the shed that won't come when called, standing long and entering into good, he lived sweetly in the house with the jewelled woman.
2881.nuance: The jackal that won't come when called may be the unruly mind, and burning the noose the ending of bonds. ஆயிழை (the jewelled woman) is often taken as Shakti. The syntax is loose and the reading tentative.

2882.reading: When rain falls on the mountain the fawn leaps and the ripe fruit on the bunch falls; the smith set the nectar to pour onto the breast as onto a piece on the forge.
2882.nuance: Tradition reads the mountain as the head, the rain as the nectar that flows from it in yoga, and the smith as the Lord or the yogi. The forge image (உலை) suggests heat that releases the flow. The fawn and the fruit are unexplained.

2883.reading: In the Brahmin's house there are five milch cows that roam wild with no one to herd them; if a herdsman comes and their wildness is checked, the Brahmin's five cows will pour milk.
2883.nuance: The five cows are widely taken as the five senses, and the closer chapter on restraining them (2025) uses the same herdsman. The point is that the senses, once herded, give milk: restraint makes them yield, not die. The herdsman may be the guru or the disciplined mind.

2884.reading: Five wild cows, thirty lions, two sweet mangoes with nine long peppers: if one holds them as one's own monkey, they are within one's mind; if the unageing buffalo is let loose, they set it ablaze.
2884.nuance: The numbers suggest a count of tattvas or bodily powers, but I can't map them. குரங்கொளில் and மூவாக் கடா (the unageing buffalo, perhaps death or the mind) are obscure, and the last line may be corrupt.

2885.reading: As an unschooled maiden reads aloud the meaning of the leaves of an unwritten book, so an unborn bee drank the honey from the scent of an unopened flower.
2885.nuance: Four negatives (எழுதாத, தெருளாத, மலராத, பிறவாத) make a knowing that comes before every means of knowing. It is commonly read as the soul's experience of Siva, beyond book, learning and sense; the verse states only the paradox.

2886.reading: The falsehood that goes, the false seed that enters, the fruit of the naval tree that gives gruel, the green crop standing and the five who eat it: under a burning roof they prospered.
2886.nuance: The five who eat are probably the senses, and the burning roof the body, but the first two lines (போகின்ற பொய், புகுகின்ற பொய்வித்து) may mean deeds that leave and deeds that come in as seed for birth. Very uncertain.

2887.reading: A neem rose from a bamboo shoot; on a palm leaning on the neem there is a snake; with no one to chase the snake and eat it, the neem lies there bursting.
2887.nuance: Tradition takes the bamboo as the spine and the snake as kundalini. The bursting neem, bitter and unfruitful, may be the body wasted when the serpent power is not roused. This is the tradition's key, not the verse's.

2888.reading: Ten great tigers, fifteen elephants, five skilled ones, sixteen entertainers, three worthy ones, six physicians and five at the head sit and stand there.
2888.nuance: A census of a body's or a town's inhabitants, probably standing for tattvas, breaths, senses and organs. I can't match the numbers to a known list.

2889.reading: There are two buffaloes within this town and one service for both; if both are held fast, the two buffaloes become one.
2889.nuance: The two are usually taken as the two breaths, or the right and left channels, which become one when held. The town is the body. The pattern of two becoming one is the clearest thing in the verse.

2890.reading: Setting a balance within the field of the even mind and weighing cotton in the net of devotion, with pearl as the rope, the three in the town fight daily and stand full.
2890.nuance: ஒத்த மனம் (the even mind) and பத்தி (devotion) are plain; the cotton, pearl rope and the three who fight are not. The three may be the gunas, kept in balance.

2891.reading: The owl, the snake, the parrot and the cat, the naagai and the quail live in the middle; when the owl draws near the naagai, the rat seeing the owl cries out.
2891.nuance: A household of creatures that prey on each other, probably faculties or passions in the body. நாகை is unclear (perhaps a bird or a cobra). I can't fix the code.

2892.reading: He brought three white rats that stay in the laughing, scented measure; if told to leave the forge they run and they stay; that is how those born of baseness go.
2892.nuance: The three white rats may be the three malas or the three gunas, and the forge the body or the discipline; the first line is obscure and may be corrupt. Only the three and the forge stand out.

2893.reading: Those who have entered the forest will no longer see the space of the womb; the five horses have entered the nest and the six camels the cover; if they do not enter the cover, there are the three bonds.
2893.nuance: கருவெளி (the womb-space) suggests that those who have gone in are free of birth. The five horses may be the senses and the six camels the six adharas or the inner organs; மூவணை (three yokes or three bonds) is unclear.

2894.reading: Those who set their eyes on clothing and food, oil in the tube, necklace, marriage thread and bangles sink into the pit like a fluttering cloth caught on a rock.
2894.nuance: The list is the goods of household life and of a wife's adornment, so the warning is against being taken by them. The cloth on the rock is plain enough as an image of being caught; ஆறைக் குழி (the pit, perhaps a river-pit) is unclear.

2895.reading: On the mountain where the far shore appears within the bellows, people go three times a day to offer what they have earned; there is one woman who removes the mountain that stood within afflicting them; we do not know their town.
2895.nuance: துருத்தி is a bellows and so the breath, and also the name of the shrine Tiruthuruthi; both may be meant. The one woman (ஒருத்தி) is taken as Shakti, who removes the inner obstacle. The three times a day may be the three breath-turns or the three daily rites.

2896.reading: As the kite and the parrot beat the drum, well-adorned women were married; taking form like a spirit of great penance, they rejoice in the fortune they gained.
2896.nuance: A wedding with birds for drummers. The kite and parrot may be two breaths or two powers, and the marriage a union in yoga; பூதம் may mean the elements rather than a goblin. Very uncertain.

2897.reading: What is it like when a flocking bird pecks its food and, entering into it, cuts off its food? For those who know the way of the lamp, which drinks ghee thrown on the heat and spits out soot, the fruit is easy.
2897.nuance: The second half describes a lamp: it takes in ghee and gives off black soot (மை) while giving light. Tradition may read it as the yogi who takes in and burns away. The first image is obscure.

2898.reading: No leaf, yet there is a flower; no swarm of bees here; no top, yet a root; no stalk, no cluster of flowers, yet a flower to pluck; no head to wear it; and the low-hanging branch never withers.
2898.nuance: A plant described by what it lacks, like 2885. It is commonly read as the formless reality, or the flower of inner worship that needs no head to wear it. The unwithering branch suggests what does not perish.

2899.reading: Seeing a banyan standing on the far shore, they praise the Naked One and take its fruit in the middle; the eminent, seeing the five sorrows, go there, and the worthy lie prostrate.
2899.nuance: நக்கர் is Siva as the naked one, and the banyan recalls Siva as teacher under the banyan. The far shore is release, the middle perhaps the central channel. அஞ்சு துயரம் (five sorrows) are not named.

2900.reading: By the calling river there is a hard forest two leagues long, where guarding thieves have mingled; the honest ones, chasing the guarding thieves, took back a roof that had turned back at the call.
2900.nuance: The guarding thieves (காப்பிடு கள்ளர்) are likely the senses, which seem to guard but steal, and வெள்ளர் the pure-minded who pursue them. The roof (கூரை) may be the body. Very tentative.

2901.reading: In a pond where kotti and water-lily bloom stand the bitter etti and neem and a sweet banana; those who will not eat jaggery and honey mixed together waste away for the etti fruit.
2901.nuance: எட்டி is the poisonous strychnine tree. The verse does not name what the sweet and the bitter stand for; read as a riddle, the sweet may be the Lord or true knowledge and the bitter the pleasures of sense. The plain point is choosing the bitter with the sweet at hand.

2902.reading: The female bee and the male bee, and the one who enjoyed the form of the bond under a canopy on a coloured pedestal: the last bee itself drinks, and the female bee whose eyes met it gained joy.
2902.nuance: The pair of bees may be Shakti and Siva, or the soul and the Lord; பீடிகை (pedestal) suggests an image in worship. The syntax is unclear and the reading is a guess.

2903.reading: Unless one drives the cows grazing in the field past its boundary, gathers them to the Lord's feet, works strongly and weighs one's strength, the heart that kills will not know the mark.
2903.nuance: The cows may be the senses, as in 2883, or the souls (பசு in the Siddhanta sense), led past the bounds of the world to the Lord's feet. கொல்லசெய் நெஞ்சம் (the killing heart) and குறி (the mark, the goal) are unclear.

2904.reading: A lotus bloomed in the water on a plate; a blue lily rose in the water of a deep pond; for those who can shine within the beam, a colocynth is near in the pond.
2904.nuance: Lotus and lily are common names for centres in the body; விட்டம் (beam, crossbar, or diameter) may be the space in the head. கொம்மட்டி is a bitter gourd, so the last line may be ironic. I can't fix it.

2905.reading: Six birds are within five, and a hundred birds sit on the topmost branch; after crossing the seven great cities that rise, one may enter the house without returning.
2905.nuance: The seven cities are commonly taken as the six adharas and the crown, after which one reaches the home (மனை) without change or return (மாறுதல் இன்றி). The six, five and hundred are unexplained. ஐந்தக்து is a garbled form.

2906.reading: In the well one bathes in, the round earth comes and seeps; tying it with rope and keeping it close, it becomes a light to all.
2906.nuance: கொட்டனம், வட்டனம், கட்டனம், ஒட்டனம் rhyme across the lines and their senses are unclear. I can give only the outline.

2907.reading: The seven encircling seas, the eight great mountain ranges, the deep sky with its fire, rain and wind, and the low wide earth: seeing their nature, if one thinks to live, it becomes a temple.
2907.nuance: The verse may mean that the whole cosmos is the Lord's temple, or that the body, which holds these seas, mountains and elements, is. The last line (வாழ நினைக்கில் அது ஆலயம் ஆமே) is compressed, and the third line is garbled (தன்மை ய்துகண்டு).

2908.reading: Embracing, burning the inner self, setting the furrow at the trident, they put away pride of place; after setting the staff here, the well-birds, placing their confusion here, it is the way before and after.
2908.nuance: சூலம் (trident) and கோல் (staff) may be the central channel; burning within (அகம் சுட) suggests yogic heat. The syntax of the last two lines is unclear and I can't give a reliable reading.

2909.reading: The drum and the marriage thread are two, and they say the crowbar is stronger than both; than all three, drum, thread and crowbar, they say the Lord's grace, his love, is stronger.
2909.nuance: Drum and tali are the marks of a wedding; the crowbar (பாரை) may be force or effort. The closing is plain: இட்டம் (love, favour) and ஈசன் அருள் outweigh all. What the three stand for is the tradition's guess.

2910.reading: Those who have seen a carp stay seeing; those who have seen a hare, all three are saved; one man holds the drum and the clamour, like the form a Veda has seen.
2910.nuance: கயல் (carp) is a stock image for the eye and முயல் (hare) for the moon; these may point to inner sight and the moon of yoga. The second half is obscure.

2911.reading: In a pond where sedge rose, the water-clover spread and clung; not as a heron lies in wait, the Lord settles there while the rock lies.
2911.nuance: The heron waiting for fish is a stock image of feigned stillness; the Lord's stillness is said not to be that. What the pond, sedge and rock stand for is unclear.

2912.reading: A field of three leagues and a forest of half a league: two paths lie with their boundary confused; for those who can move without confusing the boundary, passing quickly, they may enter the town.
2912.nuance: The two paths may be the two breaths or the two ways of the world and of release; keeping their boundary clear lets one reach the town, which tradition takes as Siva's abode. The measures are unexplained.

2913.reading: When ploughing and sowing are done together the rain does not fall; the lady of the wide earth embraces and works yet yields nothing; the one of growing matted hair goes on without fail.
2913.nuance: The plain image is labour without rain, effort without grace. The lady of the earth may be Shakti or the body; வளர்சடையோன் is Siva. Whether the last line means he stays unmoved or passes by is unclear.

2914.reading: The leaping tiger, even while crouching, covers twelve leagues; the tide of the cool sea that drew back flows again; the honeyed nectar wells up, and he went and surrounded the five common ones.
2914.nuance: Twelve is the traditional measure, in finger-breadths, of the outgoing breath, so the tiger may be the breath; the welling nectar is a known yogic image. The five are probably the senses, hemmed in. These are traditional keys.

2915.reading: A son grew by boarding a boat, going to sea, trading and giving; when his heart falters before Neeli, the father gives like a hailstone fruit.
2915.nuance: நீலி may be the dark goddess or a deceiving woman; ஆலிப்பழம் (hailstone) melts at once. The son may be the soul trading in the sea of births, and the father the Lord. The text may be corrupt (நீலிக்கு இறையுமே).

2916.reading: In a river three leagues long there are three banana trees, ripened in the oil-press, which bore the three impurities as fruit; and, in an obscure line, the maidens, laughing, ate the flowers and stood in the middle.
2916.nuance: திரிமலம் (the three impurities) is named outright, so the three bananas are probably the soul's three bonds. The third line (பக்கனார் மிக்கார் படங்கினார்) is obscure and may be corrupt.

2917.reading: An aaththi tree complete from root to crown, at whose tip is a three-headed bamboo; flag, weapon and the planets' arrows, five fives; the right-whorled conch came that way.
2917.nuance: ஆத்தி (bauhinia) is a garland flower of Siva, and the three-headed bamboo may be the trident or the three channels. ஐஐந்து (twenty-five) may be a tattva count. I can't give a reliable reading.

2918.reading: For the herd of little jackals lying scattered, with the pig, the snake, the cow and the monkey, after weighing them on a balance without loss, the weight is brought down to a kunri seed.
2918.nuance: The beasts may be passions or faculties, weighed and reduced to the weight of a குன்றி seed, the smallest jeweller's weight. The reading of the beasts is a guess.

2919.reading: There is a bud that rose budding; if its binding is loosed and it runs free, one can see it bloom; looking with attachment let go, so that that house falls to waste, it cannot be seen except by those who have loosed the bond.
2919.nuance: கட்டுவிட்டு (loosing the bond) frames the verse: the bud opens when untied, and only the unbound see. அம்மனை பாழ்பட நோக்கினால் is unclear; it may mean seeing the house of the body or household as empty.

2920.reading: There is green in a land watered without water, and no one can ever know it; the water that pours where the sharp rain does not fall, if you search, does not stay on high ground.
2920.nuance: Water without rain may be the inner nectar of yoga, which greens the body; that it does not stay on the high ground may mean it must be held. Very uncertain.

2921.reading: When the owl climbs the kurundham tree and practises its nature, at the time the world perceives delusion, a snake too speaks in the middle; he becomes both the mahout and the one of good nature.
2921.nuance: The snake speaking in the middle may be kundalini in the central channel and the mahout the controller of the mind. குருந்தம் is also the tree under which Siva is said to have taught Manikkavasagar. I can't fix the code.

2922.reading: The banana and the thorny soorai came and took the place, and they say the soorai is stronger than the banana; but cutting both into hard pieces, the banana takes the place and lives.
2922.nuance: The plain image is a fruitful plant and a thorny weed competing for ground, the weed thought stronger yet the banana winning. Tradition may read them as knowledge and impurity, or good and evil deeds; the verse does not say.

2923.reading: Splitting the land and driving out the long sea, the plump fish the hill-hunter of the field caught: light it up for all; if wanted it will not lessen, and it cooks without cost.
2923.nuance: The images of hunter, field and fish are mixed and the syntax is unclear. அருத்தமும் இன்றி may mean without cost or without meaning. I can give only a tentative outline.

2924.reading: In the goldsmith's house there is a child that sprouts and a conch that calls, seeking the king's bed; to the potters who rejoice and the titled men, it gives a measure, to those who examine and take it.
2924.nuance: The goldsmith's house recurs from 2876; the calling conch may be inner sound. The rest is obscure.

2925.reading: The temple buffalo left the canopy and came out; seeing the army, it turned back halfway; the owner, the minister and the townsfolk: the long gates that cannot be shut are five and four.
2925.nuance: Five and four are nine, the body's nine openings, which tradition calls its gates; the town is then the body, its owner the soul and its minister the mind. The buffalo may be the mind or death. Tentative.

2926.reading: Eight that go out and eighteen that come in made the nine gates; the snake with the eight and the four horses: if the mahout does not let go, it may even become a pig.
2926.nuance: The going and coming numbers suggest breath measures, and the nine gates the body's openings, as in 2925. பத்தெட்டு may be eighteen or ten and eight. The last line seems to warn of a low birth; I can't be sure.

2927.reading: In a pond overgrown with moss, a shy heron seeks its food and eats; when the warrior of the vanguard reaches it with his companion, the bond lies there trembling.
2927.nuance: The heron fishing in a mossy pond may be the soul feeding in the world, and the vanguard warrior death, at whose coming the bond (பாசம்) trembles. பாசம் is also Yama's noose. Tentative; பாடர்ந்து is a misprint for படர்ந்து.

2928.reading: On the pot-mountain a branch has risen, and beyond the branch a wind blows; within a flower that bloomed freshly, Isan lies as a bee and takes its fragrance.
2928.nuance: கும்பம் (pot) may be the head, or கும்பகம், the held breath; the wind beyond is the breath and the flower a centre in the head. The last line is plain: the Lord dwells as a bee in the flower. பூவக்குள் is a misprint for பூவுக்குள்.

2929.reading: The vina and its staff mingle and hum music, and the pillar too joined and filled the head; before the trade was settled, the holding there is mixed in.
2929.nuance: The vina's staff (தண்டு) is a known image for the spine, and its music for inner sound; தாணு (the pillar) is a name of Siva. The trade and holding in the last two lines are unclear.

2930.reading: It traded with those who entered Kongu; none examine and know it except when it enters the ship; they did not know that when the moon enters it becomes dark; some who entered and stayed are ascetics.
2930.nuance: திங்கள் (the moon) entering and darkness following may refer to the moon-breath or a phase of breath control. கொங்கு and வங்கு (Kongu or pollen; ship) are puns I can't resolve.

2931.reading: Dawn broke and turned golden; the two banks where punnai trees open their pollen shimmer; this is the path where the flawless Isan moves, the circle where the lady dwells.
2931.nuance: The two banks may be the two side channels with the path between them the central one, and the மண்டலம் where the lady dwells a centre of Shakti. The first line reads புலர்fந்தது, a corruption of புலர்ந்தது.

2932.reading: The people who sit with their king, desiring among themselves, set things within and bear at the door; the guide who does not leave the deathless boundary shows the way, and at our rebuke the five may be eaten.
2932.nuance: The king and people may be the soul and its faculties, the guide the guru, and the five the senses brought under rebuke. ஐந்துண்ணலாம் is unclear: the five may be enjoyed, or consumed. Very tentative.

2933.reading: When the mango in the garden has been dug out and fallen, what will calling the jackal on the edge of the land do? That is how those who kindled it, set the First One before them and showed it, let it go.
2933.nuance: காட்டிக் கொடுத்தல் is to betray or to point out; கைவிடுதல் to abandon. The verse may speak of those who showed the Lord and then forsook him, or of a teacher who shows and lets go. I can't settle it.

2934.reading: Birds cry out that dawn has come and the flowering creeper clings saying dawn has come; for the lonely man who enjoys pleasure with her in his longing, dawn has never broken.
2934.nuance: புலர்ந்தது போது (dawn has come) is repeated, and the last line denies it: புலர்ந்திலை போதே. Read as a riddle, dawn is awakening, which the pleasure-taker never meets. புலம்பன் is also the Sangam name for the hero of the seashore, so the verse borrows the love-poetry frame.

2935.reading: There is a boat to be let out at the ferry; with the woman standing pressing it and the five planting their poles, for traders on the way in the river, if the pin is shaken, this becomes that.
2935.nuance: The boat is commonly the body, the five the senses who pole it, and the ஆணி (pin, linchpin) what holds it together. வாணி may be the goddess of speech or a woman. The last phrase (அது இது வாமே) is open: the boat may become something else, or the world be lost.

links.note: Both put a single herdsman over the five (senses): 2025 has one man graze them with a staff, 2883 says that once herded and checked the five cows give milk.
The Kural guards the five with the goad of firmness and calls that man a seed for release; Tirumular herds them and they yield milk. Both make the senses useful once controlled.

The Kural says the field of the five must be destroyed (அடல், which Parimelazhagar glosses as கெடுத்தல்); Tirumular wants the five herded so they give milk. If அடல் means only 'conquer', the two agree; on the stronger reading they differ on whether the senses are ended or tamed.

Both use the man who passes over sweet fruit at hand to toil for a poor one: in 201 the jackfruit and the wild date stand for wife and another's wife; in 2901 the banana, jaggery and honey against the poisonous etti are left unnamed.
The Kural uses the ripe fruit left for the raw one for harsh speech when sweet words are at hand; Tirumular sets the sweet beside the poisonous etti, and his riddle leaves the referent open.
2872 ends with those who plough barren land with the breath-yoke; 2880 says their intent is unknowable and what sprouts in such soil may wither.
2883 has the wild cows herded so they give milk; 2903 drives the grazing cows beyond the field to the Lord's feet.
The Kural says birth is cut only when attachment is cut; Tirumular says the bud's flowering is seen only by those who have let the bond go.

935 says those who clung in pride to the dice (கவறும் கழகமும் கையும்) came to nothing. 2866 takes the same dice (கவறு ஐந்து) and makes the body the board and the Lord the player (பெருமான் இருந்து பொருகின்ற மாயக் கவறு), whose secret the poet cannot read. The pairing shows the gambler's vice of the Kural turned into an image of the Lord's hidden play in the body.

1139 says no one knows the reversed way of the nectar-breasted lady (மாறி யிருந்த வழியறி வாரில்லை), who wells up for those with inner sight. 2867 uses nearly the same line of the pure path (மாறிக் கிடக்கும் வகையறி வாரில்லை) and says love wells up (ஊறிக் கிடந்தது) for those who know it. The repeated formula, with ஊறி in both, lets 1139 name what the chapter's reversed path leads to.

126 makes the thirty-six tattvas the rungs of a ladder to release (முப்பதும் ஆறும் படிமுத்தி ஏணியாய்), climbed into inner light. 2868 sets up a ladder hard to climb (ஏறற்கு அரியதோர் ஏணி) on a palm at the junction of six streets and sees the seven seas from the top. The plain ladder of 126 offers one way to read the riddle's climb as an inner ascent.

Naladiyar 38 says a banyan seed, tiny as it is, casts vast shade, and so small virtue in worthy hands covers the sky. 2870 has an elephant grown from the seed called ஐ (ஐஎன்னும் வித்தினில் ஆனை விளைப்பது) in a field entered by the Lord's favour. The same logic of a minute seed and a huge yield works in ethics in one and in the mantra-field in the other.

41 speaks of those who praise the Lord in a heart tilled like a field (புனஞ்செய்த நெஞ்சு). 2871 says that for those who plough the field of the heart (உள்ளச்செய் உழவு செய்வார்), it grows of itself into a flooded field. Both make the heart a cultivated field; 41 says the Lord dwells there, 2871 that its yield overflows.

805 says that if the two breaths (இருகால்) are set in the upper palate there is no Death (காலனும் இல்லை). 2875 says that when the wind-cows are milked (காற்றுப் பசுக்கள் கறந்துண்ணும் காலத்து) the other cows' coming is not known (மாற்றுப் பசுக்கள் வரவு அறியோம்). If the other cows are births or changes, as is often guessed, 2875 puts 805's claim about mastered breath into the riddle's cattle images; the key is uncertain.

1946 says there is no harvest for the high (மேலோர் விளைவு) except for those who sow, and speaks of the seed within the seed. 2879 repeats விளைந்து and says the crop is seed for what is above (மேலைக்கு வித்தது), its yield spreading for those who reap again and again. Both use sowing and harvest for an inner yield reckoned 'above', and 1946's plainer wording suggests what the repeated reaping of 2879 is.

2276 says the Lord drove the jackals running (நரிகளை ஓடத் துரத்திய) and the soul's bound deeds stood and wailed. 2881 has the little jackal that won't come when called (கூப்பிடு கொள்ளாக் குறுநரி) and the noose (பாசம்) put into the fire, after which he lives sweetly in the house. In both the jackals are the unruly forces that must go before the soul settles; 2276 names deeds where 2881 names the bond.

595 says that for those who mark a boundary and make a way, it is possible to bag the monkey (குரங்கினைக் கொட்டை பொதியலும் ஆமே). 2884 lists wild cows, lions and other numbered beasts and says that if they are held as one's monkey (தாமாக் குரங்கொளில்) they are within one's mind. The caught monkey in both stands for the restless faculties brought under hand.

844 describes a lotus with no earth, no water, no stalk and no root that yet blooms, a light seen where there is no town. 2885 has an unschooled maiden reading an unwritten book and an unborn bee drinking from an unopened flower (எழுதாத, தெருளாத, மலராத, பிறவாத). Both state a direct experience by piling up negations of every means, and 844's explicit setting in yoga supports reading 2885 the same way.

151 describes death: the five who ate rice with ghee poured on it are gone (நெய்யட்டிச் சோறுண்ணும் ஐவரும் போயினார்). 2886 has the five who eat the green crop (ஐங்கூழ் அவையுண்ணும் ஐவரும்) prospering under a burning roof (வேகின்ற கூரை). The five eaters are the senses in both; 151 shows them leaving, 2886 feeding while the body-roof burns.

154 counts thirty, thirty and thirty-six who live in a walled temple and run off when it falls. 2888 lists ten tigers, fifteen elephants, five, sixteen, three, six and five who sit and stand there. Both give the body as a dwelling counted by its numbered occupants; 154 adds that they all leave when it falls.

805 says the two breaths (இருகால்) set swiftly in the upper palate open the door and keep Death away. 2889 says there are two buffaloes in this town (இரண்டு கடா) and if both are held fast they become one (ஒருகடா வாமே). Read as the two breaths, 2889 states the joining in its own image while 805 gives the place and the result.

118 praises the balance that first sets itself level and then weighs (சமன்செய்து சீர்தூக்குங் கோல்) as the ornament of the worthy. 2890 sets a balance in the field of the even mind (ஒத்த மனக்கொல்லை உள்ளே சமன்கட்டி) and weighs in the net of devotion. The same levelled scale is the image of fairness in the Kural and of the steadied mind in 2890.

2916 names its three: three banana trees that bore the three malas as fruit (திரிமலம் காய்த்தன). 2892 has three white rats (வெள்ளெலி மூன்று) brought to the forge, said to be born of baseness (புலைக்குப் பிறந்தவை). 2916's open naming of திரிமலம் is the chapter's own support for reading 2892's three as the three impurities.

126 says that if one draws in the five like a tortoise in one birth it guards for seven births. 2893 says that once the five horses have entered the nest (கூடுபுக்கு ஆனது ஐந்து குதிரையும்) those who have gone in will no longer see the womb-space (கருவெளி). Both tie drawing in the five senses to freedom from birth; 2893 makes it an end of birth, not a protection.

919 says the soft shoulders of women of fine jewels (மாணிழையார்) are the mire (அளறு) in which base men sink (ஆழும்). 2894 says those who set their eyes on clothing, food, oil, ornaments, marriage thread and bangles sink into a pit (ஆறைக் குழியில் அழுந்துகின்றார்). Both picture desire for adorned things as sinking in mud; the Kural's object is the courtesan, 2894's the goods of household life.

218 says that for those who know how the tall flame fed by ghee (நெய்நின்று எரியும் நெடுஞ்சுடர்) burns, the darkness (மை) loosens. 2897 says the fruit is easy for those who know the way of the lamp that drinks ghee and spits out soot (நெய்யுண்டு மைகான்று). Both use the ghee lamp and its மை as a figure for burning away darkness, and 218 explains the riddle's lamp.

844 says there is no earth and no water yet a lotus, no stalk and no root yet it bloomed. 2898 says there is no leaf yet a flower, no top yet a root, no stalk yet a flower to pluck, and the branch never withers. Both describe a flower defined by what it lacks; 844 adds that it is known only through hearing (கேள்வியிற் பூவே).

2087 speaks of what the holy one under the banyan's shade (கல்லால் நிழல் புண்ணியன்) taught the four. 2899 has people see a banyan on the far shore (அக்கரை நின்றதோர் ஆல மரம்), praise the Naked One and take its fruit. The banyan of Siva as teacher in 2087 helps read the riddle's tree as the place of his teaching.

1823 makes the body a temple and turns the thieving five senses (கள்ளப் புலன்ஐந்தும்) into its lamps. 2900 has guarding thieves (காப்பிடு கள்ளர்) in a forest, chased by the honest ones who take back the roof. Both call the senses thieves; 1823 converts them while 2900 drives them off.

536 likens the ritualist beside the knower to one who eats bitter things while ghee, milk and curd stand at hand (நெய்பால் தயிர்நிற்க). 2901 says those who will not eat jaggery and honey mixed waste away for the bitter etti fruit. Both make the same complaint, choosing the bitter with the sweet at hand; 536 says plainly who does it.

2193 says the cows are many-coloured but the herdsman is one, and when he lays down his staff they will not let go of their master (தலைவனைப் பற்றி விடாவே). 2903 says the cows grazing in the field must be driven past the boundary and gathered to the Lord's feet (இறையடிக் கூட்டி). Both picture the cows brought to cling to their Lord.

1823 makes the heart the great temple and the body of flesh the shrine. 2907 lists the seven seas, eight mountains, sky, fire, rain, wind and earth and says that, seeing their nature, if one thinks to live, it becomes a temple (ஆலயம் ஆமே). 2907 extends 1823's temple from the body to everything the body and world are made of.

3038 says the Lord stood as the tall mountains and the seven seas (நெடு மால்வரை ஏழ்கடல்) and as the earth below and above. 2907 lists the same seven seas and great mountain ranges and the elements, and calls them a temple (ஆலயம்). Both treat the whole cosmos as where the Lord is; 3038 says he is it, 2907 that it is his shrine.

380 asks what is stronger than fate (ஊழிற் பெருவலி யாவுள), which comes first whatever one devises. 2909 sets drum, marriage thread and crowbar against each other and says the Lord's grace and love is strongest of all (இட்டம் வலிதென்பர் ஈசன் அருளே). If ஊழ் and grace are taken as rival answers to what is strongest, the two claims conflict; 2909 does not name fate, so the tension depends on that reading.

591 tells the yogi to wait like a heron at the sluice-mouth (மடைவாயிற் கொக்குப்போல்) and so last an aeon. 2911 says the Lord settles in the pond not as a heron lies in wait (நாரை படுக்கின்றாற் போலல்ல). 591 makes the heron's watch a model for practice; 2911 limits it, saying the Lord's stillness is not that watchful, aiming kind.

490 says to fold up like a heron when the time calls and strike like it when the moment comes (கொக்கொக்க கூம்பும் பருவத்து). 2911 says the Lord rests in the pond not as a heron lies in wait. The Kural takes the heron's waiting-to-strike as a model of timing; 2911 uses the same image to mark what the Lord's stillness is not.

595 says that for those who mark out a boundary and make a way (வரம்பினைக் கோலி வழிசெய்குவார்க்கு) the monkey can be bagged. 2912 says two paths lie with their boundary confused and those who move without confusing it (எல்லை மயங்காது) reach the town. Both make keeping a boundary the condition of the way through.

619 says that even if fate denies the end, effort pays the wage of the body's labour (மெய்வருத்தக் கூலி தரும்). 2913 says that when ploughing and sowing are done the rain does not fall and the earth, though she works, yields nothing (தான்பய வாது). On the reading that 2913 shows labour without grace bearing no fruit at all, it denies the wage the Kural promises.

880 says the mind joined with the breath binds the five senses (ஐம்புலன் கட்டுண்ணும்) and they drink unfading nectar (அமுதமே). 2914 says the honeyed nectar wells up (ஆரமுது ஊற) and he went and hemmed in the five (ஐவரைப் போய்வளைத்தான்). The same pair, nectar and the five brought to bay, appears in both; 880 states it plainly.

2159 says that within waking the fourteen jackals ate poison and died (நரிகள் பதினாலு நஞ்சுண்டு செத்தன). 2918 has a herd of little jackals (சிறுநரிக் கூட்டம்) with other beasts, weighed until their weight is brought down to a kunri seed. Both use a pack of jackals for the faculties that must be ended or reduced.

879 says to cut a thorn tree while young, since grown hard it destroys the cutter's hand. 2922 says the thorny soorai is thought stronger than the banana, yet when both are cut to pieces the banana takes the place and lives. Both turn on the strength of the thorn plant; the Kural fears it, while 2922 shows the fruitful plant outlasting it once both are cut.

152 describes death: all nine gates are shut together (ஒன்பது வாசலும் ஒக்க அடைத்தன). 2925 speaks of the long gates that cannot be shut, five and four (அடையா நெடுங்கடை ஐந்தொடு நான்கே). Both count the body's nine openings; 2925 shows them open in life, 152 shut at its end.

194 likens the life to a bee that goes to flowers and drinks their scented honey. 2928 says Isan lies within a fresh flower as a bee and takes its fragrance (வண்டாய்க் கிடந்து மணங்கொள்வன் ஈசனே). The same bee-and-flower image is the soul's restless seeking in 194 and the Lord's dwelling in 2928.

607 lists the inner sounds, sea, cloud, elephant, the vina (வீணை), flute and conch, known only to the yogi. 2929 says the vina and its staff mingle and hum music (வீணையும் தண்டும் விரவி இசைமுரல்). 607's list supports reading 2929's vina as the inner sound of yoga.

2883 says the Brahmin's five cows roam wild with no herdsman, and when one comes and checks them they give milk. 2932 has a guide who keeps the deathless boundary and shows the way (வழிகாட்டி), at whose rebuke the five may be eaten (ஐந்துண்ணலாம்). 2932 gives 2883's herdsman the role of a guide and repeats that the checked five become usable.

1687 says the unripe do not know the dawning and will not open their eyes even when it dawns (விடிவது அறியார்). 2934 says birds and creeper announce dawn, but for the one who enjoys pleasure in his longing it has never dawned (புலர்ந்திலை போதே). Both say dawn comes and some never wake to it; 2934 names pleasure as what keeps them asleep.

In 1329 the lover wishes the night would last so he may go on pleading (நீடுக மன்னோ இரா). 2934 borrows the same love-poetry frame, the man with the woman for whom dawn never breaks (புலர்ந்திலை போதே), but turns the endless night into a fault. The pairing shows Tirumular reversing the Kural's wish.

Thiruppugazh 785 says the soul shut in the body-house is whipped by three lashes and driven like a boat on the sea (கடல் ஓடம் அது என). 2935 has a boat at the ferry with five planting their poles (ஐவர்கோல் ஊன்றல்) and warns that if the pin is shaken this becomes that. Both picture the body as a boat pushed by outside powers.

source_issues: 2931 line 1: புலர்fந்தது contains a Latin f; read புலர்ந்தது (marked CORRUPT_LINES).
2874 line 2: ஓர்ஏழுளு ஐந்துள, probably ஓர் ஏழுள ஐந்துள.
2876 line 1: அசுத்தில் is probably அகத்தில் (compare தட்டான் அகத்தில் in 2924).
2905 line 1: ஐந்தக்து is garbled, perhaps ஐந்தகத்து.
2907 line 3: தன்மை ய்துகண்டு is garbled, probably தன்மை அது கண்டு.
2927 line 1: பாடர்ந்து is a misprint for படர்ந்து.
2928 line 3: பூவக்குள் is a misprint for பூவுக்குள்.
2884 line 4, 2892 line 1, 2915 line 3 and 2916 line 3 are obscure and may be corrupt.
